name: Congenital Coronary Artery Aneurysm

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Congenital Coronary Artery Aneurysm Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Identification of coronary artery dilation exceeding 1.5 times the normal diameter on imaging
Evidence of aneurysm present from birth or early infancy without acquired causes
Exclusion of secondary causes such as Kawasaki disease, atherosclerosis, or connective tissue disorders
Presence of cardiac symptoms such as angina or arrhythmias supportive but not mandatory

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of coronary artery aneurysm on imaging with congenital onset and exclusion of acquired causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on imaging and clinical history to exclude acquired etiologies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Coronary artery aneurysm detected by angiography
searchTerms: enlarged heart artery seen on angiogram

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital coronary artery dilation confirmed by echocardiography
searchTerms: dilated heart artery from birth on ultrasound
heart artery enlargement seen by echo

occasional.symptomName: Fatigue related to decreased cardiac output
searchTerms: fatigue due to low cardiac output

occasional.symptomName: Signs of myocardial ischemia on ECG
searchTerms: signs of heart muscle lack of oxygen on ECG

rare.symptomName: Myocardial infarction in infancy or early childhood
searchTerms: heart attack in baby or young child

laboratory: Normal autoimmune panels (to exclude connective tissue disorders)
imaging: Cardiac MRI for detailed vessel wall assessment
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; possible association with connective tissue disorder genes in rare cases
other: Electrocardiogram abnormalities consistent with ischemia or arrhythmia

distinguishingFeatures: Systemic vasculitis with fever and mucocutaneous inflammation
Typically adult onset with cardiovascular risk factors
Presence of atherosclerotic plaques on imaging
Presence of systemic connective tissue disorder signs (e.g. Marfan syndrome)
Genetic testing positive for connective tissue disorder mutations

redFlags: Sudden onset chest pain in infant or child
Signs of myocardial infarction or ischemia
references: Maron BJ, et al. Congenital coronary artery aneurysms: clinical features and management. Circulation. 2020.
Orphanet Report on Congenital Coronary Artery Aneurysm, ORPHA:95491.
Kawasaki T, et al. Coronary artery aneurysms in children: differential diagnosis and treatment. J Pediatr Cardiol. 2019.
